job.title: People & Culture Business Partner
job.description:
The Opportunity
An established Australian family owned organisation with a national footprint is seeking an experienced People & Culture Business Partner to support its South Australian business.

This is a broad, hands-on HR partnering role offering considerable autonomy and exposure across the full employee lifecycle. Working closely with senior leaders and as part of a national People & Culture function, you will act as the key P&C contact for the South Australian business, balancing strategic partnering with the delivery of pragmatic, commercially focused HR solutions.

The environment is fast-paced and operational, so this opportunity will suit someone who enjoys being close to the business, building credibility with leaders and employees, and taking ownership rather than operating within a highly segmented HR model.

The Role
Partnering with leaders across the business, you will provide advice, coaching and support across a diverse range of people matters. You will build trusted stakeholder relationships and help strengthen leadership capability while ensuring national people initiatives are effectively embedded locally.
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Providing operational HR advice and coaching to leaders across the employee lifecycle.
  • Managing complex employee and industrial relations matters, including workplace investigations and performance issues.
  • Playing an active role in enterprise bargaining, including preparation, stakeholder engagement, and implementation.
  • Supporting workforce planning, recruitment, onboarding and retention strategies.
  • Coaching leaders on performance management, development and effective people leadership.
  • Supporting organisational change and transformation initiatives.
  • Providing guidance on employment legislation, industrial instruments, policies and procedures.
  • Contributing to the development and implementation of broader national People & Culture projects and initiatives.
  • Using workforce insights and data to identify trends and support better people and business decisions.
About You
You will be an experienced HR generalist who is comfortable operating autonomously and can move confidently between strategic conversations and hands-on employee matters.

Ideally, you will bring:
  • 3+ years' experience in an HR Business Partner or comparable generalist HR position.
  • Tertiary qualifications in Human Resources, Business Management or a related discipline.
  • Sound knowledge of Australian employment legislation, workplace relations and contemporary HR practices.
  • Practical experience managing employee relations and industrial relations matters.
  • The confidence to coach and influence leaders at different levels of an organisation.
  • Strong stakeholder management, communication and relationship-building capability.
  • The ability to navigate change, ambiguity and sensitive workplace matters with sound judgement.
  • A commercial and pragmatic approach, with the ability to use data and insights to inform decisions.
  • The ability to work independently while remaining closely connected to a broader national HR team.
Experience within transport, logistics, manufacturing, warehousing, infrastructure, engineering or another operational/industrial environment would be particularly valuable.

Why Consider This Opportunity?
This is an excellent opportunity for an HR professional looking for genuine ownership and breadth. Rather than specialising in one area of HR, you will work closely with the business across the full spectrum of people matters, while having access to the expertise and support of a national P&C function.

You will have the opportunity to guide and influence leaders, navigate ER/IR matters, contribute to enterprise bargaining and change initiatives, and help shape the people agenda within the South Australian operation.

If you enjoy being visible in the business, building trusted relationships and delivering practical HR solutions, this is an opportunity to make a tangible impact.

The Role

  • Manager the end-to-end enterprise bargaining process across four Enterprise Agreements.

  • Work closely with senior leaders in the business and client sites to ensure all details are covered .
  • Drive agreements through to successful conclusion, including approval and implementation.
  • Support when needed on ER and IR more broadly in the business bargaining risks and stakeholder expectations throughout the process
About You
You will be an HR professional experienced  in ER/IR enterprise bargaining and, importantly, successful outcomes in union negotiations.
You will bring:
  • Demonstrated end-to-end experience leading and negotiating Enterprise Agreements.
  • A proven track record of working directly with unions and navigating and supporting operational leaders through the process
  • Current knowledge of Australia's industrial relations framework and contemporary bargaining environment.
  • Experience within heavy industry, utilities, mining, manufacturing or a similarly complex operational environment.
  • A pragmatic, commercially minded approach, you get things done and come with a glass half full approach

A 15 -month fixed-term opportunity to make a tangible contribution to four important enterprise bargaining processes, bringing specialist expertise and experience to a business navigating a significant period of industrial relations activity.
